problem: RL-based indoor navigation agents (e.g., SAVN) rely on RGB alone, need lots of data and adapt poorly to new scenes; existing meta-learning approaches need many hand-designed tasks.
motivation: Humans use meta-skills and rich perception to solve new tasks quickly. The paper argues that richer visual information (segmentation, depth, object regions) from a single monocular RGB camera, plus attention and memory, should improve target-driven navigation and adaptation. It also proposes voice commands as the goal specification.
key_idea: Extend SAVN with multimodal aggregation of RGB, segmentation, depth and object-region features (with region self-attention) fed to an LSTM policy, trained with self-supervised MAML-style meta-learning and a voice-command target.
insight: Adding extra visual modalities to RGB consistently beats the RGB-only SAVN baseline, and combining segmentation with region features gives the best overall result (SPL 17.27, SR 48.70 vs 13.86/40.20). Self-attention on region features gives a small gain on 'All' (SPL 15.26→16.04, SR 46.00→46.50) but not on the L>=5 subset. Gains are modest and there is no separate ablation of the meta-learning component.
method: Auditory encoder: wav2letter++ transcribes the voice command and NLTK extracts the target noun; the target is embedded with GloVe.
Visual encoders: ResNet-18 RGB feature, DeepLab segmentation feature, MonoDepth depth feature, Faster-RCNN (ResNeXt-101, Visual Genome) top-7 region features plus 4-d box proposals.
Multi-processors: each feature is converted into an aggregatable tensor (A-Tensor) via linear or conv layers with ReLU, with per-feature architectures given in a table.
Multimodal aggregation: A-Tensors are concatenated, passed through a pointwise conv and reshaped into an embedding e; an LSTM (hidden size 512) outputs the action policy and value.
Region attention: self-attention with a two-layer linear scoring network and softmax weights over the 7 region features.

Meta-learning (SAVN/MAML-style): a learned self-supervised interaction loss L_int^phi updates the policy over the first k steps, and the navigation loss (+5 for finding the object, -0.01 per step) is optimized on the remainder of the trajectory.

setting.backbone: SAVN-based LSTM policy with frozen pretrained ResNet-18, DeepLab, MonoDepth and Faster-RCNN encoders; wav2letter++ for speech
setting.training_data: AI2-THOR SAVN dataset: 4 room types x 30 rooms, 20 train / 5 val / 5 test per type; pretrained feature extractors on ImageNet, Visual Genome, Cityscapes, KITTI
setting.observation: monocular first-person RGB (depth, segmentation and detection derived from RGB by pretrained networks) plus voice command

numbers.eval_set_note: 1000 episodes (250 per room type); the paper says 'validation results' but also mentions test rooms
numbers.backbone: SAVN + RGB, segmentation and region features
numbers.extra: meta-learning; success = target within 1 m and in view when Done is issued

numbers.backbone: SAVN + RGB, segmentation and region proposals
SAVN + RGB and attended region features
numbers.evidence: Table: Quantitative results (%), row 'Region (Feature) with Self-Attention'

numbers_note: Only the single-authored AI2-THOR benchmark is reported; the inference-time results appear only in a figure. Baseline SAVN row: SPL 13.86, SR 40.20.
results: All multimodal variants beat the RGB-only SAVN baseline (SPL 13.86, SR 40.20). The best, Segmentation + Region (Feature), reaches SPL 17.27 and SR 48.70; on L>=5, Segmentation + Region (Proposal) gets SPL 14.86 and SR 30.90. The authors also claim faster inference (shown only in a figure).
limitations: Evaluated only on AI2-THOR against a single baseline (SAVN) with modest gains; no real-robot experiments.

Voice is handled by an off-the-shelf ASR plus noun extraction from clean commands, so the 'voice' component is not truly evaluated; there is no ablation isolating meta-learning or attention rigorously.
Depth and segmentation networks are pretrained on outdoor datasets (Cityscapes, KITTI), which may not transfer well to indoor scenes.
